prompt: A software company moved from a one-time license of $1,200 to a $40-a-month subscription. New customers rose 50%, but first-year revenue per customer fell 60%. Which is the strongest initial hypothesis?

options.text: The lower entry price is likely attracting more customers, and the subscription will pay off if they stay over 30 months.
options.feedback: Right. It commits to a likely cause that fits the facts, and it is testable: I'd model retention by cohort.

options.text: It could be price, retention, sales, marketing or product changes.
options.feedback: This lists several causes without committing to the most likely one.

options.text: The subscription switch was a mistake and the company should go back to licenses.
options.feedback: This states a cause as certain before any data has tested it.

options.text: Customers are responding to the new model.
options.feedback: This is too vague to test: it doesn't say what is wrong or what data would show it.

explanation: $40 a month equals the $1,200 license after 30 months. The switch pays off if retention is long enough, which cohort data can show.

distractor_flaws.M.shotgun_hypotheses: It could be price, retention, sales, marketing or product changes.
distractor_flaws.M.overconfident_hypothesis: The subscription switch was a mistake and the company should go back to licenses.
distractor_flaws.M.untestable_hypothesis: Customers are responding to the new model.
